candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registri (platni promet) hub page
candidates.why_relevant: Single hub the Central Bank of Montenegro maintains under the Law on Payment Transactions (Zakon o platnom prometu) linking all four statutory payment-side registers: payment systems, payment institutions + agents, e-money institutions + agents, and revoked authorisations. This is the root node from which the entire ME payments actor map can be enumerated.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly HTTP fetch of the hub page, diff the four child links and their attached PDFs; treat added/removed entities as events.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search (sr) on regulator register terminology
queries_used: CBCG registar platnih institucija i institucija elektronskog novca Crna Gora

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registar platnih institucija i njihovih agenata
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative list of every licensed payment institution (platna institucija) in Montenegro, plus registered account information service providers (AISP), branches, and agents. Directly enumerates the competitor and partner universe for payment services in ME.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch page + linked 'Pregled registra' PDF monthly; parse entity name, licence number, licence date, services authorised, agent list; snowball each entity name into cells covering vendors/competitors.
candidates.discovered_via_method: sr search + snowball from CBCG registri hub
queries_used: CBCG registar platnih institucija i institucija elektronskog novca Crna Gora

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registar institucija za elektronski novac i njihovih agenata
candidates.why_relevant: Statutory register of e-money institutions (institucije za elektronski novac) authorised to issue e-money in ME, with branches and agents. Identifies wallet/prepaid/fintech actors that do not appear in the bank register.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly page + PDF fetch and diff; extract entity, licence date, agent network.
candidates.discovered_via_method: sr search + snowball from CBCG registri hub
queries_used: CBCG registar platnih institucija i institucija elektronskog novca Crna Gora

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registar platnih sistema (payment systems / operators)
candidates.why_relevant: Register of licensed payment systems and their operators in ME — the closest official enumeration of clearing/settlement and card-scheme-adjacent infrastructure operators. Page explicitly offers a 'Pregled registra' PDF download.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download the 'Pregled registra' PDF each quarter; parse system name + operator; cross-reference operators against CRPS for ownership.
candidates.discovered_via_method: fetched CBCG registri hub and followed child link
queries_used: CBCG registar platnih institucija i institucija elektronskog novca Crna Gora

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Spisak platnih institucija i institucija za elektronski novac kojima je oduzeto odobrenje
candidates.why_relevant: Negative register: licences withdrawn. Essential for churn/exit signals and for avoiding stale actor lists; a withdrawal is itself a market event worth tracking.

candidates.discovered_via_method: sr search result + hub snowball

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registar banaka (register of credit institutions)
candidates.why_relevant: Statutory register of licensed credit institutions, third-country and EU branches and representative offices in ME. The definitive buyer/competitor list for core banking, cards and payments vendors; each bank has its own child page with details.

candidates.why_relevant: Index of CBCG-supervised non-bank providers: leasing companies, factoring, purchase-of-receivables firms, microcredit financial institutions and credit guarantee funds. Expands the licensed-actor map beyond banks/PIs into adjacent lending and BNPL-like players.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated CBCG register of card processors / card-acquiring processors or ATM operators was found as a distinct published list. Searches in sr for processing and exchange-office terminology returned only the four payment-side registers plus the bank register.
negative_findings.result_summary: Card processing appears to be covered implicitly, either inside the 'registar platnih sistema' (system operators) or as an authorised service line within the payment-institution register, rather than as a separate list.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Cell #9's remit explicitly names card processors; if no discrete register exists, downstream cells cannot derive processor actors from a register and must infer them from payment-system operator entries plus CRPS activity codes.

negative_findings.description: Search for a register of authorised exchange offices ('registar ovlašćenih mjenjača', 'mjenjački poslovi') on cbcg.me returned no such list.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only the payment registers and generic financial-system pages were returned; no exchange-office register surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Exchange offices are a cash-handling channel adjacent to payments; their absence from the enumerable set is a coverage limitation to state explicitly rather than assume away.

negative_findings.description: The guessed English-language CBCG URL https://www.cbcg.me/en/key-functions/payment-system/registers/register-of-payment-institutions-and-their-agents returned HTTP 404.
negative_findings.result_summary: CBCG does not use translated English URL slugs; the English tree reuses the Montenegrin slugs under an /eng/ prefix (confirmed by an observed /eng/kljucne-funkcije/... bank-register URL).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any crawler built on translated English paths will silently miss the entire English mirror. Locale handling must be prefix-swap, not slug translation. This is a URL-construction failure, not evidence the English register is missing.

negative_findings.description: The IRMS tax-portal business-entity register search rendered no content to a plain HTTP fetch.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only the 'IRMS Portal' shell was returned; the register UI is client-side rendered.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Recorded as unverified/hypothesis, not dead. It likely has an underlying JSON API that would be the best structured collection route for ME company data — worth a headless-browser investigation.

negative_findings.description: For both the Capital Market Authority (scmn.me) and the Insurance Supervision Agency (ano.me), the existence of a licence register was confirmed in their own descriptive material, but the direct public register URL was not established in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Regulator homepages and rules pages located; register deep-links not located.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These two supervisors cover investment firms and insurers, adjacent buyer segments. Leaving them at homepage granularity weakens the completeness claim of the licensed-actor index.

negative_findings.description: No public structured member directory ('imenik članova') was located for Privredna komora Crne Gore despite a targeted sr-language search.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only institutional pages (about, boards, contact) surfaced; no searchable member database.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The chamber would otherwise be the natural industry-side cross-check on the ICT vendor population; without it, vendor enumeration depends more heavily on CRPS activity codes.

negative_findings.description: data.gov.me was confirmed to exist as a national open-data portal, but no specific CRPS, CBCG-register or licensed-institution dataset was confirmed to be published there in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Portal and a 'uprava' dataset group were located; the presence of a machine-readable company or licence register dataset remains unverified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If such a dataset exists it would replace fragile HTML/PDF scraping with a legal, structured feed. Its absence would mean all register collection must be scrape-based.

coverage_gaps.description: Card processors / payment processors and ATM-network operators have no dedicated ME register; they must be inferred from payment-system operator entries, payment-institution service lines, and CRPS NACE codes.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Download the 'Pregled registra' PDF from the payment-systems register and manually classify each operator; then run CRPS activity-code sweeps for J62/J63 and K66 to catch processors registered as IT firms.

coverage_gaps.description: Every register found is an HTML page or a PDF; no confirmed bulk download, API or CSV extract for CRPS company data or for the CBCG licence registers.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe the IRMS SPA's XHR endpoints, the crps.me /preuzimanja/pregled downloads area, and data.gov.me's CKAN-style dataset API before committing to a scraping architecture.

coverage_gaps.description: Two parallel company-register front-ends were observed (pretraga.crps.me under CRPS, and irms.tax.gov.me under the Revenue and Customs Administration). Which is canonical going forward is unresolved.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Establish which endpoint the authority treats as canonical and pin collection to it; monitor crps.me notice pages for a migration announcement.

coverage_gaps.description: SCMN (capital market) and ANO (insurance) licence registers were confirmed to exist but not located at URL level.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a site-scoped crawl of scmn.me and ano.me for 'registar' / 'licence' / 'dozvole' paths and add the concrete register URLs.

coverage_gaps.description: No mapping was built from KD 2010 / NACE Rev.2 activity codes to the payments-and-banking-technology segments of interest, so CRPS and MONSTAT activity-based enumeration cannot yet be executed precisely.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Obtain the MONSTAT KD 2010 classification, fix the target code set (K64/K66 financial services and auxiliary activities, J62/J63 IT services), then run CRPS searches by code.

coverage_gaps.description: CBCG serves the same content under at least four locale prefixes (/me/, /eng/, /r/, /c/) and at least one register exists under both a correct and a misspelled slug ('insitucije').
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build the CBCG URL inventory from https://www.cbcg.me/r/mapa-sajta rather than by hand, and deduplicate entities across locale variants before diffing.

coverage_gaps.description: It is unclear how much of the CRPS beneficial-ownership register is publicly readable versus gated behind a qualified digital certificate.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test an anonymous lookup on eFirma; if gated, document the legal access route rather than treating ownership data as unavailable.

coverage_gaps.description: Local-language (sr/Montenegrin) coverage was strong and drove nearly every discovery; English-language searching added almost nothing new beyond the exchange and CBCG mirror pages, and no EU-level register (EBA/ECB) covers Montenegro since it is not an EU member state.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Keep collection sr-first; use English CBCG mirrors only for entity-name normalisation. Do not expect EU passporting registers to enumerate ME actors.

brief: Montenegro's licensed-actor index is unusually clean and concentrated: the Central Bank of Montenegro (cbcg.me) publishes, under statute, a bank register plus four payment-side registers (payment systems, payment institutions and agents, e-money institutions and agents, and revoked authorisations) and a non-bank financial-service-provider index covering leasing, factoring, microcredit institutions and guarantee funds — together these enumerate essentially every regulated banking and payments actor in the country. Legal-entity resolution, ownership and activity codes then come from CRPS, the Central Register of Business Entities, via pretraga.crps.me and the eFirma portal (with a beneficial-ownership register since Aug 2021), while MONSTAT's Statistical Business Register supplies the KD 2010 / NACE Rev.2 population counts needed to size the vendor and financial-sector universe. Two structural cautions dominate: everything is HTML pages and PDFs with no confirmed bulk extract or API, and a second company-register front-end (irms.tax.gov.me, JavaScript-rendered, tax administration) runs in parallel with CRPS, so the canonical endpoint should be settled before building collection. Card processors have no register of their own and must be inferred from payment-system operator entries plus CRPS activity codes; SCMN and ANO registers are known to exist but were not pinned to a URL in this pass.
